title: My early AI-coded Web game is now an AI-coded Watch game: Doomscroll
author: ironicsans
selftext:
A little more than a year ago, before the current generation of vibe-coding tools really kicked things up a notch, I vibe-coded a web game I called [Doomscroll](https://gisnep.com/doomscroll/) to scratch an itch I had to see if I could make a fun game that you plan only by scrolling. I also wrote [an article](https://ironicsans.ghost.io/doomscrolling-the-game/) about how I developed the game. The game and article were a hit, making the front page of [HackerNews](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45205232), where a lot of the discussion was around this being an example of vibe-coding to actually make something novel and not just slop. Of course, now this kind of thing isn’t very novel anymore!

Fast forward a year. I like games on my Apple Watch, but recently I was growing a bit tired of the Watch games I have, and I wished people would make more games for the Watch. But there just aren’t that many games that can be easily played just by turning the Digital Crown. I thought,people should make more games you can play just by turning the Crown.

And then I realized: *Wait a minute.* *I already made a game you could play by just turning the Crown! Doomscroll!*

So then I used Fable to convert my web game into [an Apple Watch game](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/doomscroll-scroll-or-die/id6791591956). With a bit of work, it ended up being a fairly faithful conversion. I had to remove a couple features that just didn’t work at such a small size, but that was a platform limitation, not a Watch limitation.

I had never put anything on the app store before, so it was partly an exercise to learn how to do that. I don’t expect to make money from this.

If anyone would like to check it out, below are a few free codes. And if you just want to try the game without a watch, you can play it free on the website.
